metadata.name: LoCoMo Benchmark Dataset (Sample)
metadata.description: Long Context Conversations with Memory — evaluation benchmark for memory-augmented dialogue systems.
metadata.paper: Maharana et al., ACL 2024 — Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
metadata.note: This file contains a representative sample of 5 conversations with 60 QA pairs across 4 categories for local evaluation. Download the full dataset via: datasets.load_dataset('snap-stanford/locomo')

qa_categories.single_hop: Questions answerable from a single conversation turn
qa_categories.multi_hop: Questions requiring reasoning across multiple turns
qa_categories.temporal: Questions about when events occurred or their sequence
qa_categories.adversarial: Questions designed to trick memory systems (unanswerable or negation)

published_baselines.description: Scores reported in Maharana et al. 2024 (Table 4, ROUGE-1 / F1 on full test set)

conversations.persona: Alex, a software engineer who loves cooking and hiking

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: I just got back from a hike at Mount Rainier. It was absolutely exhausting but worth it.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That sounds amazing! How long was the trail you did?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: We did the Wonderland Trail loop, about 35 miles over 3 days. My hiking partner Jake came along.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Impressive! 35 miles in 3 days is no small feat. Did Jake enjoy it too?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: He did, though he twisted his ankle on day 2. We still made it though. I'm already planning the next one.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Oh no, hope Jake is okay! Where are you thinking for the next adventure?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Thinking about the John Muir Trail in California. But first I need to get my new hiking boots broken in.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: I've been experimenting with sourdough bread lately. Made my third loaf yesterday.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: How did the third loaf turn out compared to your first two?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Much better! The crust was perfect. I used a Dutch oven this time instead of a baking sheet.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Dutch ovens make a huge difference. Are you using a starter you made yourself?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Yes, I named it 'Bubbles'. It's 6 weeks old now. My friend Sarah gave me the original culture from hers.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Love the name! How often are you feeding Bubbles?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Once a day now, down from twice. I keep it in the fridge when I'm not baking.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Big news — I got promoted to Senior Engineer at work today!

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Congratulations! That's a huge achievement. How are you feeling about it?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Excited and a bit nervous. I'll be leading the payments infrastructure team.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Leading a team is a big step. Do you have much experience managing people?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Some — I mentored two interns last summer. But this is my first formal leadership role.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: You'll do great. Are you planning to celebrate?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Yeah, going out for dinner with my partner Sam and calling my parents tonight.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: I finally did the John Muir Trail! Just got back two days ago.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: You mentioned planning that back in January! How was it?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Incredible. 211 miles in 21 days. Harder than Rainier but more beautiful.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Did Jake come along on this one?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: No, his ankle never fully healed. I went solo this time, which was a whole different experience.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Solo through 211 miles — respect. Did you feel safe out there?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Mostly yes. I had a satellite communicator. Ran into trouble with a bear on day 8 near Muir Pass though.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Had to put my sourdough starter on hold. Been too busy since the promotion.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Ah, poor Bubbles! Is the starter still alive or did it not make it?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: It's in the fridge in hibernation mode. I dried some as backup. It's been about 2 months.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Smart to dry some backup. How's the team lead role going?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Stressful but rewarding. We shipped a major feature last week — real-time payment notifications.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That sounds like a significant milestone. How did the team respond?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Really well. I'm planning a team lunch to celebrate. Thinking of cooking something myself, maybe use this as the excuse to revive Bubbles.

qa_pairs.question: What trail did Alex hike at Mount Rainier?
qa_pairs.answer: The Wonderland Trail loop

qa_pairs.question: What is the name of Alex's sourdough starter?
qa_pairs.answer: Bubbles

qa_pairs.question: What team does Alex lead after their promotion?
qa_pairs.answer: The payments infrastructure team

qa_pairs.question: Did Jake join Alex on the John Muir Trail?
qa_pairs.answer: No, Jake's ankle never fully healed after the Mount Rainier hike so Alex went solo.

qa_pairs.question: Why did Alex stop maintaining their sourdough starter?
qa_pairs.answer: Alex got too busy after being promoted to Senior Engineer and team lead.

qa_pairs.question: Did Alex do the John Muir Trail before or after getting promoted?
qa_pairs.answer: After — the promotion was in April 2023 and the JMT was completed in June 2023.

qa_pairs.question: How old was Bubbles the sourdough starter when Alex first mentioned it?
qa_pairs.answer: 6 weeks old

qa_pairs.question: Who gave Alex the sourdough culture for Bubbles?
qa_pairs.answer: Their friend Sarah

qa_pairs.question: How many people did Alex mentor before becoming team lead?
qa_pairs.answer: Two interns, during the previous summer.

qa_pairs.question: What feature did Alex's team ship and what is the connection to the promotion celebration plan?
qa_pairs.answer: They shipped real-time payment notifications. Separately, Alex plans to celebrate with a team lunch and use it as an excuse to revive the sourdough starter Bubbles.

conversations.persona: Maria, a nurse who recently moved cities and is learning to paint

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: I just moved to Chicago from Austin last week. Still living out of boxes.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Big move! What brought you to Chicago?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: A new position at Northwestern Memorial Hospital. I'm a nurse and they offered me a critical care role.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Impressive — critical care nursing is demanding work. Are you settling in okay?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Slowly. My cat Luna is stressed and hiding under the bed. I miss my sister Rosa back in Austin.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: I signed up for a watercolor class at the Chicago Arts Center. First session was last Tuesday.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: How was the first class?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Humbling. I struggled with washes but the instructor, Professor Chen, was very patient.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Watercolor is notoriously tricky. Did you have any art background before?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: None at all. I wanted something completely different from nursing. A way to decompress.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That makes total sense. Did you make any friends in the class?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Yes, a woman named Fatima. She's a retired teacher. We got coffee after class.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Luna finally came out from under the bed. Only took 4 months!

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Ha! Cats on their own timeline. Has she fully settled in now?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: She's claimed the window seat and watches the pigeons. Very content.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Classic cat. How's the painting going?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Finished my 6-week course and signed up for the intermediate level. Professor Chen said I've made real progress.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Rosa finally visited from Austin! She stayed for a week.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That must have been wonderful — you mentioned missing her when you first moved.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: It was exactly what I needed. We did all the touristy things — Millennium Park, the Art Institute.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Did she get to see your paintings?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Yes! I've done about 20 now. She actually wants to buy one — the one I did of Lake Michigan at sunrise.

qa_pairs.question: Where did Maria move from?
qa_pairs.answer: Austin

qa_pairs.question: What is the name of Maria's cat?
qa_pairs.answer: Luna

qa_pairs.question: How long did it take Luna to come out from hiding after the move?
qa_pairs.answer: 4 months

qa_pairs.question: Who is Maria's painting instructor and what did they say about her progress?
qa_pairs.answer: Professor Chen at the Chicago Arts Center said Maria had made real progress after the 6-week course.

qa_pairs.question: What painting does Rosa want to buy?
qa_pairs.answer: The one Maria painted of Lake Michigan at sunrise.

conversations.persona: Dev, a grad student studying climate science who runs marathons

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: I just registered for the Boston Marathon. It's in April — gives me 10 weeks to train.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Boston! That's a qualifier-only race. Impressive you made the cut.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Barely — I qualified with a 3:04 at Chicago last fall. Boston cutoff was 3:05 for my age group.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: One minute to spare! What's your goal for Boston?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Sub-3 hours. Ambitious but I think my training block can get me there.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Hit a snag — developed IT band syndrome last week. Had to cut back training.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Frustrating timing so close to Boston. How bad is it?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: My physio Dr. Reyes says I can race if I manage it carefully. Ice, stretching, and no tempo runs for now.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: At least it's manageable. How's the PhD research going alongside training?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: My climate model finally converged after 3 weeks of debugging. Advisor Professor Kwan is happy.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: I ran Boston! Finished in 3:07.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Amazing! Given the IT band issue, how do you feel about 3:07?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Honestly, thrilled. The IT band flared at mile 20 but I pushed through. Missed sub-3 but it was my second best ever.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Your second best — what was your best?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: 3:04 at Chicago. Which is also my qualifier. So really I'm just chasing that time back down.

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Defended my dissertation chapter 3 today. Passed with minor revisions.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Congratulations! Which chapter was this — the climate model one?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Yes, my Arctic sea ice projection model. Professor Kwan called it the strongest chapter.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's excellent validation. Are you planning your next marathon yet?

turns.speaker: human
turns.text: Yes — Chicago again in October. Going for a PR. Fully healthy now, no IT band issues.

qa_pairs.question: What was Dev's finishing time at Boston Marathon?
qa_pairs.answer: 3 hours and 7 minutes (3:07)

qa_pairs.question: Did the IT band syndrome develop before or after registering for Boston?
qa_pairs.answer: After — Dev registered in February and the injury developed in March.

qa_pairs.question: What is Dev's personal best marathon time and where did they set it?
qa_pairs.answer: 3:04 at the Chicago Marathon, which also served as the Boston qualifier.

qa_pairs.question: What is Dev's dissertation research about?
qa_pairs.answer: Arctic sea ice projection (climate science / climate modeling)

qa_pairs.question: Who is Dev's physio and what advice did they give?
qa_pairs.answer: Dr. Reyes — advised ice, stretching, and no tempo runs while managing IT band syndrome before Boston.
